standard.title: Develop Inquiry Questions
standard.description: develop questions to investigate a contemporary economic and business issue
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have developed questions about people, events, developments, places and systems in primary HASS (AC9HS6S01). They can form basic inquiry questions but have not yet applied economic and business concepts and vocabulary systematically to question construction, nor targeted their questions specifically at contemporary issues.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students develop questions to investigate a contemporary economic and business issue.

nodes.label: What makes a question investigable
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can distinguish between open, investigable questions and closed or unanswerable questions in an economic and business context.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify one investigable and one non-investigable question about an economic topic; explain the difference.
nodes.typical_width: Distinguish between closed, leading and open investigable questions in economics and business; explain what makes a question useful as the basis for an investigation (e.g. answerable using data/evidence, economically relevant, contemporary); apply to provided examples.
wider: Examine why the same economic situation (e.g. rising prices, a new business opening) can generate multiple different investigable questions depending on the investigator's perspective or purpose
Analyse a sample student investigation and evaluate whether its driving question was investigable — and what a better question might have been
nodes.hinge_reason: Students who cannot distinguish investigable from non-investigable questions will produce driving questions that cannot be meaningfully answered with data or evidence — the entire investigation phase collapses if the question is circular, too narrow, or unanswerable.

response_modes.reason: The distinction between a question and an investigable question is not obvious at Year 7. Scaffold by working through examples: 'Is scarcity real?' is not investigable; 'How does our school allocate its limited resources to meet student needs?' is. Students need to see and evaluate the contrast before generating their own.

success_criteria: Identifies a question as investigable or not-investigable and gives a reason
Explains at least two features of a good investigable question

nodes.label: Using economics concepts in question construction
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can develop questions using economic and business concepts and terms such as scarcity, opportunity cost, market, income, goods and services.
nodes.minimum_width: Develop one question using at least one economic or business concept correctly; the question must be investigable.
nodes.typical_width: Develop questions using a range of economic and business concepts and terms — scarcity, opportunity cost, market, income, business, goods and services, costs and benefits — framed as investigable questions about contemporary issues; refine questions to ensure they are answerable using accessible data or sources.
wider: Develop a set of linked sub-questions that unpack a complex economic issue — practising how a main investigation question can be broken into component investigable questions
Peer-review a partner's question set using an explicit criterion checklist for economic vocabulary, investigability and contemporary relevance
Develop questions specifically about a First Nations economic context (e.g. 'How does the Gumatj Corporation decide how to allocate its resources?') and evaluate their investigability

response_modes.reason: Students need practice generating and revising questions across multiple economic topics before the skill becomes transferable. Provide question stems that prompt concept use ('How does... affect...?', 'What is the opportunity cost of...?') and have students adapt them to different issues.

success_criteria: Develops at least one investigable question that correctly uses an economics or business concept
The question is answerable using accessible data or sources
